                      MARK ALLAN BRADBURY'S Letter of support for ﬁling 6670


November 17, 2026

Public Utility Commission of Texas
1701 N. Congress Avenue
Austin, Texas 78701

Re: PUC Docket No. 59475 — Support for John B. Bradley III’s Veriﬁed Request for Disclosure on the
Record and Conditional Motion for Recusal of Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson (Item No. 6670)

Dear Chairman Gleeson and Commissioners:

I am writing in support of John B. Bradley III’s Veriﬁed Request for Disclosure on the Record and
Conditional Motion for Recusal of Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson, ﬁled November 10, 2026, as Item No.
6670 in PUC Docket No. 59475.

Mr. Bradley’s request raises legitimate questions concerning the transparency and impartiality of the
Commission’s proceedings regarding the proposed Bell County East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV
transmission line. These questions deserve a complete and documented response before the
Commission makes its ﬁnal determination on the Certiﬁcate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN).

1. Disclosure of the December 16, 2025 Transmission Roundtable

According to the October 27, 2026 POLITICO reporting cited in Mr. Bradley’s motion, a closed-door
meeting identiﬁed as a “Transmission Roundtable” occurred on December 16, 2025, involving
representatives of the Governor’s Office, ERCOT, electric transmission companies, and major technology
companies.

The reported attendee list included Chairman Gleeson and representatives of Oncor Electric Delivery
Company, an applicant in this proceeding.
 The meeting occurred after the Commission had assigned development responsibility for the Import Path
2 transmission facilities and during the development of the related CCN applications.

Although the meeting’s actual discussions have not been established, its reported participants, subject
matter, and timing raise reasonable questions about whether the proposed 765-kV transmission
projects, including Import Path 2, were discussed outside the public contested-case process.

I support Mr. Bradley’s request for disclosure on the record of Chairman Gleeson’s attendance and
participation, together with the meeting agenda, relevant communications, meeting notes, and any
discussion concerning the necessity, development, routing, or regulatory approval of the proposed
Import Path 2 facilities.

2. Preservation of Impartiality and Procedural Fairness

Under 16 Texas Administrative Code § 22.3(f)(1), a commissioner must recuse himself from a proceeding,
or from deciding particular issues, when the commissioner lacks impartiality or the commissioner’s
impartiality has been reasonably questioned.

The standard does not require proof of actual bias before questions concerning impartiality may be
appropriately examined.

I recognize that communications between government officials, utilities, and industry representatives are
not inherently improper. However, communications concerning disputed facts or legal issues in an actual
or anticipated contested proceeding warrant careful scrutiny, particularly when the participants include a
decision-maker and representatives of an applicant seeking regulatory approval.

The Commission’s decision must be based on the evidentiary record and applicable law, not on
undisclosed discussions with parties having a direct ﬁnancial interest in the outcome.

Accordingly, I support Chairman Gleeson’s recusal from further substantive participation in Docket No.
59475, including deliberations and voting, if the disclosed facts establish that his impartiality has
reasonably been questioned under the applicable rule.

3. Particular Importance of the Commission’s Remanded Issues

The concerns raised by Mr. Bradley are especially signiﬁcant because the Commission previously
remanded this proceeding to the State Office of Administrative Hearings for additional ﬁndings
concerning Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13.

Those issues concern whether the proposed facilities are necessary to meet state or federal reliability
standards and the estimated congestion cost savings to consumers.

These are central questions in determining whether the Applicants have established the need for the
proposed transmission facilities.

If the December 16, 2025 meeting included discussions of Import Path 2, its asserted necessity,
projected demand, economic justiﬁcation, or anticipated approval, such discussions could be directly
relevant to the impartiality concerns raised in Mr. Bradley’s motion.
 The Commission should establish whether any such discussions occurred before Chairman Gleeson
participates in further substantive consideration of these issues.

4. Protection of Landowners and Public Conﬁdence

The proposed 765-kV transmission project would impose substantial and potentially permanent
consequences on affected Texas landowners, including transmission easements, potential
condemnation of property rights, impacts on agricultural operations, and changes to the use and
enjoyment of private property.

These consequences make transparency and procedural fairness particularly important.

Landowners who participate in the Commission’s proceedings are entitled to conﬁdence that their
evidence and arguments receive impartial consideration and that Applicants do not receive an
undisclosed opportunity to inﬂuence decisions concerning project necessity or approval.

A complete public accounting of the December 16, 2025 meeting would help preserve that conﬁdence
and allow the Commission to resolve the questions raised by Mr. Bradley through an appropriate,
documented process.

5. Requested Commission Action

I respectfully request that the Commission:

   1. Grant Mr. Bradley’s request for appropriate disclosure on the record concerning Chairman
      Gleeson’s attendance and participation in the December 16, 2025 meeting, including any
      discussions relevant to Import Path 2 or Docket No. 59475.

   2. Make available, to the extent authorized by law, relevant agendas, attendance records,
      communications, notes, and other records identifying the subjects discussed.

   3. Determine whether any communications concerned disputed facts or legal issues relevant to the
      proposed transmission facilities and whether those communications implicate applicable ex
      parte or impartiality requirements.

   4. Require Chairman Gleeson to recuse himself from further participation in Docket No. 59475,
      including deliberations and votes, if the established facts satisfy the recusal standard under 16
      TAC § 22.3.

   5. Permit Mr. Bradley to supplement his motion after receiving responsive public information
      records, consistent with applicable Commission procedures.

Conclusion

I support Mr. Bradley’s motion because the integrity of the Commission’s proceedings requires that
reasonable questions concerning potentially relevant, undisclosed communications be addressed
openly and fairly.
 This letter does not allege that Chairman Gleeson engaged in misconduct or that any prohibited ex parte
communication has been established. Rather, it requests disclosure sufficient to determine whether
recusal is warranted under the Commission’s rules.

The public, affected landowners, and all parties to this proceeding deserve a decision reached through a
transparent and impartial process.

Thank you for your consideration.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Mark Allan Bradbury
Pro Se Intervenor
PUC Docket No. 59475
504 Grand Ave
Brady, TX 76825
